source.title: On the universality of neural encodings in CNNs

record.tranche_reason: The study measures similarities between learned weight-covariance eigenspaces across independently trained CNNs, including networks with different initializations and training tasks. This is a conceptual test of convergence across seeds and of partial, task-dependent convergence, using weight-based measures rather than the original representation-comparison approach.
record.gate_note: Results cited from other studies are not recorded. The study's own comparisons of learned spatial and channel eigenvectors and covariance similarities are recorded; the figures show layer- and rank-specific curves, while the text gives several aggregate descriptions rather than exact values.
record.test_reason: The study compares learned weight covariances and their eigenvectors, after activation-based Procrustes alignment, across CNNs trained from different seeds, on different datasets and with true or random labels. This bears directly on V3 (seeds) and on V7 (partial, task-dependent convergence). Its spatial-eigenvector results also bear on V5. It uses a different method from the originals (weights rather than activations).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors conclude that VGG-type CNNs show a seemingly universal encoding of natural images: spatial eigenvectors are universal across filter size, depth, dataset and task, and channel eigenvectors are shared, to a lesser extent, across datasets over a range of layers, vanishing in task-specific deeper layers. True-label and random-label training yield two distinct encoding strategies; random-label realizations share one. They claim this explains transfer learning and propose maximizing universality to build foundation models.
record.recipe_differences: Compares aligned weight covariances and their eigenvectors rather than relying on representation-similarity measurements alone; introduces factorized CNNs with frozen spatial filters and learned channel weights.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported channel similarities vary with task and depth: true-label versus random-label networks correlate weakly, while similarities across datasets gradually vanish deeper in the networks.
record.peer_reviewed: To appear at the ICLR 2024 Workshop on Representational Alignment (Re-Align)
record.problems: The study uses a single VGG-type architecture for the reported comparisons and does not test model scaling or capability. Many results are presented as figures without exact numerical values in the text. The comparisons do not establish that common training data or objectives cause the observed similarities.

untested.parts: No sweep over model size or capability; one VGG-type architecture only.
Procrustes alignment is used as a tool; mapping loss or stitching performance between models is not reported.
Convergence is not compared across alternative similarity measures, settings or out-of-distribution inputs.
Only VGG-type CNNs and one seed pair on ImageNet-32 are tested; individual-unit matching is not quantified beyond the Figure 2 illustration.
No neurons, SAE features or circuits; only spatial covariance eigenvectors, judged by visual inspection.
Whether alignment plateaus is not tested; whether a common model of reality versus shared data drives the effect is not separated.

missing.what: Comparison of seed-pair eigenvector cosine similarities with and without activation-based alignment on CIFAR10. Without alignment, layer-2 eigenvectors are not aligned, showing shared subspaces but not shared bases. Also shows performance comes from the correlated rank range.
Effective rank of the learned covariances rises with depth and with number of classes or dataset diversity.
The first layer shows different spatial eigenvector behaviour from layers 2 and deeper.

record.verdict_notes: Single architecture family (VGG-11 variants). Most channel results are figure-only, with no numbers in the text except the ~0.2 true-versus-random correlation. The comparison is weight-based, but its alignment step relies on activation similarity, so it is not independent of representation similarity. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No scaling sweep or comparison of model size or capability.
No vision-language or paired image-caption comparison.
Tests weight-covariance eigenvectors and covariances for CNNs; does not test whether the same individual units or bases are learned.
Uses activation-based Procrustes alignment to compare weights, but does not test whether one model's representations can be mapped to another's with little loss.
Does not test recurrence of interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
Does not compare the convergence results across alternative similarity measures, settings, or out-of-distribution inputs.
Compares datasets and label tasks, but does not establish whether shared data or objectives, rather than a common model of reality, cause the similarities.

rows.measure: Similarity of learned spatial eigenvector patterns
rows.value: A similar canonical set of spatial eigenvectors is reported across filter sizes, datasets, and tasks, including random labels.
rows.note: The text also notes distortions with random labels and noisier patterns at lower image resolution.
rows.check: Uses standard (unfactorized) VGG with different datasets, filter sizes and tasks, so it is not a seed comparison. It shows the same visualizable spatial eigenvector set recurring across trained models, which bears on V5. The evidence is visual and qualitative, with distortions under random labels.

tranche.reason: The study investigates convergence using aligned weight covariance eigenvectors and normalized covariance similarity, providing a different measurement approach to the same question.

source_check.notes: Several pack values are ellipsized; judgments cover their visible claims. Random-label experiments in Figures 3–4 retain augmentation and batch normalization but use quadrupled training time, so the task comparison does not isolate label choice alone.

statements.correction: Factorized VGGs share channel encoding over an appreciable range of layers across datasets, including disjoint ImageNet class subsets; similarity gradually vanishes deeper in the networks. Shared training examples are unnecessary for the reported early-to-middle-layer similarity. Architecture and classification objective remain shared. V7 label=limits_scope for this condition group.
statements.problem: The disjoint-dataset result is accurately described, but challenges overstates its implication for V7, which also allows shared objectives and incomplete convergence.
